history.summary: The principal temple of the Pushtimarg (Vallabh Sampradaya) Vaishnavite tradition. The black-marble idol of Shrinathji — Krishna as a seven-year-old lifting Govardhan hill — was originally worshipped at Jatpura/Govardhan near Mathura. Fleeing Aurangzeb's temple destruction in the 1660s, the priests carried the idol via Agra; at Sinhad village on the Banas river the cart's wheels sank in mud and would not move, taken as the Lord's will to stay. Maharana Raj Singh of Mewar gave refuge and the temple was built in 1672 by Goswami Damodar Das Bairagi. Nathdwara ('Gateway to Shrinathji') became the sect's seat; the Tilkayat head priests are descendants of Vallabhacharya. Designed on the lines of Nanda Maharaj's temple in Vrindavan (hence Nandalaya/Nanda Bhavan), with seven flags atop the shikhara for the seven houses of Pushti Marg. The town is the home of the Pichhwai painting tradition depicting Shrinathji's leelas. CSV district implied Nagaur is wrong — Nathdwara is in Rajsamand district (corrected, flag).

name: Shrinathji Temple
town_description: Nathdwara ('Gateway to Shrinathji') is a town in Rajsamand district, Rajasthan, in the Aravalli hills on the Banas river, 48 km north-east of Udaipur; it is the religious seat of the Pushtimarg sect and famed for its Pichhwai miniature painters.

travel.railway: Mavli Junction (~30 km; nearest major station)
travel.road: 48 km north-east of Udaipur on the Udaipur-Rajsamand highway; well connected by road

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Janmashtami, Holi and Annakut are the grandest festivals
visitor_information.opening_hours: Eight daily darshans (Mangala, Shringar, Gwala, Rajbhog, Uthapan, Bhog, Aarti, Shayan); temple closes between darshans. Timings vary seasonally — check the current schedule before visiting. Mobile phones, socks and shoes not allowed inside; lockers near the gate.
